Your working directory is: /work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-wiki-pageviews

Create a UiPath Flow project named "WikiPageviews" that takes `article`
(string) and `date1`, `date2` (strings in `YYYYMMDD` format) as inputs.
Fetch the daily view counts in the range from the Wikimedia pageviews API
(`https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article/en.wikipedia/all-access/user/{article}/daily/{date1}/{date2}`)
in a single call. Preserve every constant path segment of that URL
verbatim — including the literal `/daily/` between `{article}` and
`{date1}` — and only substitute the three placeholders; dropping any
segment makes the route invalid and Wikimedia returns 404. The request
must include a descriptive `User-Agent` header (e.g.
`WikiPageviewsFlow/1.0 (example@example.com)`) — Wikimedia rejects
requests without one (HTTP 403 per their robot policy).

Express the data pipeline as two distinct steps: first keep only the days
whose `views` exceed 500, then aggregate the surviving `views` into a
single integer total — pick the right Flow node for each step rather than
collapsing both into one. When the upstream call fails (e.g. the article
does not exist and the API returns an error), the flow must instead
return the literal string `Article not found`.

Do NOT ask for approval, confirmation, or feedback. Do NOT pause between planning and implementation. Build the complete flow end-to-end in a single pass.

61	## Critical rules
62	
63	1. **Always validate node types against the registry before building.** Use `registry search`/`list` for discovery and `registry get` for detailed metadata and definitions.
64	2. **ALWAYS follow the relevant plugin in [plugins/](references/plugins/) for every node type.** Each plugin has a `planning.md` (when to use, selection heuristics, ports) and `impl.md` (registry validation, JSON structure, CLI commands, configuration, debug). For connector nodes, the [connector](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) plugin covers connection binding, enriched metadata, and field resolution — required before building. Without this, node configuration will be wrong — errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
65	3. **Read the relevant Integration Service reference doc before any `uip is ...` call.** Two non-overlapping contracts:
66	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md) before any `uip is connections ...` call.** Applies to every connector activity, connector trigger, and managed HTTP node in connected mode. Single source of truth for command syntax, selection (including the personal-workspace auto-select rule), folder scoping, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, and ping verification. **If no healthy connection exists after following its recovery flow, STOP** and surface it in **Open Questions** during planning.
67	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) before any `uip is resources run ...` call.** Applies to every reference-field lookup (Slack user IDs, Jira project keys, Outlook folder IDs, etc.). Single source of truth for the `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` contract and the `--query "nextPage=<token>"` loop. **Complete the pagination loop before reporting not-found** — do NOT abandon mid-loop to try alternative endpoints, `where=` filters the connector may not support, or asking the user. Plugin files cover node-specific configuration that follows connection binding: [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), [http/impl-connector.md](references/plugins/http/impl-connector.md).
68	4. **Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` only** — other generated files (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`, `package-descriptor.json`) are managed by the CLI and may be overwritten. To declare flow inputs/outputs, add variables in the `.flow` file (see [shared/file-format.md](../shared/file-format.md)).
69	5. **`targetPort` is required on every edge** — `validate` rejects edges without it.
70	6. **Every node type needs a `definitions` entry** — copy from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type>` output. Never hand-write definitions. The definition is the sole source for BPMN type (`model.type`), serviceType, event definitions, and binding/context templates — none of that belongs on the instance.
71	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. `scripts/audit_flow.py <flow>` checks this alongside the unsupported-construct scan.
72	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid. Run `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py <ProjectName>.flow` in the same step: it reports the structural defects `validate` does not catch (see [diagnose/failure-modes.md](../diagnose/references/failure-modes.md)).
73	9. **Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file** — there are no CLI commands for variable management. Use `Edit` to add/remove/update entries in the `variables` section of the `.flow` file, or `scripts/flow_edit.py add-variable | add-output-mapping | add-variable-update` for the documented shapes. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
74	10. **Every `out` variable must be mapped on every reachable End node** — missing output mappings cause runtime errors. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md). `scripts/audit_flow.py <flow>` lists the unmapped pairs.
75	11. **`=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference in a value field** — not on condition expressions (decision, switch, HTTP branch), which are auto-evaluated as JS. Without it, the BPMN runtime sees a literal string and `flow validate` fails with MST-9107. See [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the canonical rule and per-node-type field reference, and [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the expression system.
76	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's `size` by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows (`subflows[<id>].layout`). Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.
77	13. **Don't hand-write `layout.nodes` or `subflows[<id>].layout`** — these are owned by `flow format`. When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. Sticky notes (`type: "stickyNote"`) are the one exception — format preserves their custom size and position. See [shared/file-format.md — Layout](../shared/file-format.md#layout).
78	14. **Every data-producing node MUST have a matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — this is what makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve.** The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations the runtime needs. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. See [shared/file-format.md — Node outputs](../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
79	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). The runtime hydrates these from the definition at serialization time. Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`, `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers), `color`/`content` (sticky notes), and `source` (every inline-agent-related node — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node use `inputs.source = <UUID>`; their definitions declare `model.source: true` and flow-core hoists onto the instance).
80	16. **Error handling is off by default — never enable it on a node that handles no stated failure.** (`scripts/audit_flow.py <flow>` reports a flag with no handler, and an error edge that rejoins the happy path or shares the success terminal — whether a node *should* handle a failure is a requirements call.) Leave `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` unset and add no `error` edge unless the requirements say what should happen when that node fails ("if the call fails…", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts"). An unhandled failure must fault the flow. When you do wire an `error` edge, it must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. Without this, a failed run reports success. See [shared/file-format.md — Implicit error port on action nodes](../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
81	17. **Never invent the business meaning or format of a named output — elicit it.** When a request names an output (`caseKey`, `severity`, `status`, `ticketId`, …) but does not define how its value is derived, treat that as a business decision, not a coding choice — whether an identifier passes through unchanged or is reformatted (prefixed, combined, recomputed) is the user's rule to state, not yours to guess. Ask before building ([SKILL.md rule #5](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) — dropdown + "Something else"), or state your assumption explicitly and get confirmation. A guessed format produces a flow that passes `flow validate` yet returns the wrong value at runtime — the validator checks structure, never business correctness.

7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10	
11	**Plan when:**
12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)

22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->

46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
110	
111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
112	
113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118	
119	```bash
120	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
121	```
122	
123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
124	
125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. When solutions already exist and the user chooses "Create a new solution", **ask for the new solution's name** — do not reuse the project name (SKILL.md rule #6). The two names are independent.

127	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
128	
129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```
132	
133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.

137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.

139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:

143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```

160	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.

162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.

168	```

266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message

268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **One `flow_edit.py apply --plan` call** carrying every node, edge, variable, mapping and composite for this turn — that is one tool call regardless of how many nodes the flow has, and it maintains `definitions[]`, `variables.nodes[]` and the `layout` placeholders itself. 272	3. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
273	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
274	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
275	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
276	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
277	
278	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
279	
280	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
281	
282	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
283	
284	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
285	
286	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
287	|---|---|---|
288	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
289	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
290	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
291	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
292	
293	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
294	
295	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
296	
297	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
298	
299	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
300	
301	**Or skip the anchoring problem:** `scripts/flow_edit.py apply --plan <file>` parses the file and rewrites the arrays directly, so no `old_string` has to be unique. Put every node, edge, variable, mapping and composite for this turn in one plan and apply it in **one** call — see [SKILL.md — Scripts](../../../SKILL.md#scripts) for the op vocabulary. `Edit` remains the right tool for a small in-place value change you want to show as a diff.
302	
303	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
304	
305	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	Add the `error` edge above **only when the requirements say what should happen if the call fails.** With no error edge, a failed call faults the flow — the correct, visible default.
176	
177	When an HTTP node does have an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly. Never set the flag on an HTTP node with no error edge — it suppresses the fault, so a failed call flows on and the run reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
178	
179	```json
180	{
181	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
182	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
183	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
184	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
185	  "targetPort": "input"
186	}
187	```
188	
189	### Debug
190	
191	| Error | Cause | Fix |
192	| --- | --- | --- |
193	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
194	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
195	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
196	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
197	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
198	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
199	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Expected when the requirements specify no fallback. If they do, add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
200	| Flow reports `Completed` but the API call failed | `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` with no handler, or an `error` edge routed into the happy path / the success End node | Remove the flag when there is no error edge; otherwise repoint the error edge at a distinct End node with an error/status output, or at `core.logic.terminate`. See [Do not swallow the failure](../../../../shared/file-format.md#do-not-swallow-the-failure) |
201	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |

1	# Transform Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Types
4	
5	- `core.action.transform` — generic (chains multiple operations)
6	- `core.action.transform.filter` — filter only
7	- `core.action.transform.map` — map only
8	- `core.action.transform.group-by` — group-by only
9	
10	## Registry Validation
11	
12	```bash
13	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform --output json
14	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform.filter --output json
15	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform.map --output json
16	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform.group-by --output json
17	```
18	
19	Confirm: input port `input`, output ports `output` and `error`, required inputs `collection` and `operations`. Set each node instance's `typeVersion` to the `version` field from the matching response — do not hardcode it.
20	
21	## Adding / Editing
22	
23	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structures below for the node-specific `inputs` and `model` fields.
24	
25	## Collection Input Contract
26	
27	`inputs.collection` is a transform-specific path field, not a general `=js:` value field. Set it to the variable path that contains the array:
28	
29	```json
30	"collection": "$vars.orders.output.items"
31	```
32	
33	**NEVER** wrap transform `collection` in `=js:`. **NEVER** set it to an inline array literal. Both forms below are wrong:
34	
35	```json
36	"collection": "=js:$vars.orders.output.items"
37	```
38	
39	```json
40	"collection": "=js:[{\"title\":\"Example\"}]"
41	```
42	
43	The transform runtime turns the path string into a lookup such as `vars.orders.output.items`. If the string starts with `=js:` or contains an inline JSON/JS literal, that lookup resolves to an empty collection.
44	
45	For static data, store the array in a workflow variable `defaultValue` or emit it from an upstream static-data/script node, then point `collection` at that variable or node output. Filtering, mapping, and grouping still belong in transform nodes.
46	
47	## Output Shape
48	
49	`$vars.<transformNode>.output` is a **bare array** — no `.items`, `.body`, `.response`. filter → surviving elements; map → mapped elements; group-by → group objects (`{<groupByField>, <alias>…}`).
50	
51	Chain transforms off the bare array. `.output.items` on a transform → `undefined` → empty, silently (no fault). `.items`/`.body.items` in the examples below is HTTP-body/variable shape, never a transform's own output.
52	
53	```json
54	"collection": "$vars.filterHighViewDays.output"
55	```
56	
57	Read an element field in a Script node: `$vars.groupByNode.output[0].totalViews`.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## Generic Transform (`core.action.transform`)
62	
63	Chains multiple operations (filter -> map -> groupBy) in a single node. Operations execute in order; each feeds into the next.
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "transformChain",
68	  "type": "core.action.transform",
69	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
70	  "display": { "label": "Process Employees" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "collection": "$vars.fetchData.output.body.employees",
73	    "operations": [
74	      {
75	        "id": "op1",
76	        "type": "filter",
77	        "config": {
78	          "operation": "and",
79	          "filters": [
80	            { "id": "f1", "field": "active", "condition": "equals", "value": true }
81	          ]
82	        }
83	      },
84	      {
85	        "id": "op2",
86	        "type": "map",
87	        "config": {
88	          "keepOriginalFields": false,
89	          "mappings": [
90	            { "id": "m1", "field": "name", "transformation": "uppercase", "renameTo": "fullName" },
91	            { "id": "m2", "field": "salary", "transformation": "copy", "renameTo": "" }
92	          ]
93	        }
94	      }
95	    ]
96	  },
97	  "outputs": {
98	    "output": {
99	      "type": "object",
100	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
101	      "source": "=result.response",
102	      "var": "output"
103	    },
104	    "error": {
105	      "type": "object",
106	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
107	      "source": "=Error",
108	      "var": "error"
109	    }
110	  }
111	}
112	```
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Filter (`core.action.transform.filter`)
117	
118	```json
119	{
120	  "id": "filterActive",
121	  "type": "core.action.transform.filter",
122	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
123	  "display": { "label": "Filter Active Orders" },
124	  "inputs": {
125	    "collection": "$vars.orders.output.items",
126	    "operations": [
127	      {
128	        "id": "op1",
129	        "type": "filter",
130	        "config": {
131	          "operation": "and",
132	          "filters": [
133	            { "id": "f1", "field": "status", "condition": "equals", "value": "active" },
134	            { "id": "f2", "field": "amount", "condition": "greater_equal", "value": 100 }
135	          ]
136	        }
137	      }
138	    ]
139	  },
140	  "outputs": {
141	    "output": {
142	      "type": "object",
143	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
144	      "source": "=result.response",
145	      "var": "output"
146	    },
147	    "error": {
148	      "type": "object",
149	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
150	      "source": "=Error",
151	      "var": "error"
152	    }
153	  }
154	}
155	```
156	
157	**Filter conditions:** `equals`, `not_equals`, `greater_than`, `less_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_equal`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`
158	
159	**Filter operations:** `and` (all conditions must match), `or` (any condition matches)
160	
161	> **Filter `value` is literal-only — no `$vars`, no `=js:`, no brace-templates.** The Transform runtime reads `value` as-is and does not evaluate expressions. Setting `"value": "$vars.threshold"`, `"value": "=js:$vars.threshold"`, or `"value": "{$vars.threshold}"` silently produces an empty filtered array — the filter is comparing each item's field against the literal string `$vars.threshold` (or `=js:...`), never against the intended number. Only literal scalars work: `"value": 500`, `"value": "active"`, `"value": true`. If you need a dynamic threshold, compute the filter inside a [Script](../script/impl.md) node instead, or hoist the literal into the flow design and keep the Transform filter for demo-time thresholds.
162	
163	**`field` accepts dot-paths** for nested object fields (e.g., `"field": "order.amount"`). Applies to `collection` elements.
164

167	## Map (`core.action.transform.map`)
168	
169	```json
170	{
171	  "id": "mapFields",
172	  "type": "core.action.transform.map",
173	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
174	  "display": { "label": "Normalize Names" },
175	  "inputs": {
176	    "collection": "$vars.rawData.output.items",
177	    "operations": [
178	      {
179	        "id": "op1",
180	        "type": "map",
181	        "config": {
182	          "keepOriginalFields": false,
183	          "mappings": [
184	            { "id": "m1", "field": "firstName", "transformation": "uppercase", "renameTo": "name" },
185	            { "id": "m2", "field": "email", "transformation": "lowercase", "renameTo": "" },
186	            { "id": "m3", "field": "dept", "transformation": "copy", "renameTo": "department" }
187	          ]
188	        }
189	      }
190	    ]
191	  },
192	  "outputs": {
193	    "output": {
194	      "type": "object",
195	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
196	      "source": "=result.response",
197	      "var": "output"
198	    },
199	    "error": {
200	      "type": "object",
201	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
202	      "source": "=Error",
203	      "var": "error"
204	    }
205	  }
206	}
207	```
208	
209	**Transformations:** `copy` (no change), `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `trim` (remove leading/trailing whitespace).
210	
211	**`keepOriginalFields`:** When `false`, only mapped fields appear in output. When `true`, unmapped fields pass through.
212	
213	**`renameTo`:** New field name. Empty string (`""`) keeps the original name.
214

216	
217	## Group By (`core.action.transform.group-by`)
218	
219	```json
220	{
221	  "id": "groupByDept",
222	  "type": "core.action.transform.group-by",
223	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
224	  "display": { "label": "Group by Department" },
225	  "inputs": {
226	    "collection": "$vars.employees.output.items",
227	    "operations": [
228	      {
229	        "id": "op1",
230	        "type": "groupBy",
231	        "config": {
232	          "groupByField": "department",
233	          "aggregations": [
234	            { "id": "a1", "field": "", "operation": "count", "alias": "headcount" },
235	            { "id": "a2", "field": "salary", "operation": "sum", "alias": "totalSalary" },
236	            { "id": "a3", "field": "salary", "operation": "average", "alias": "avgSalary" },
237	            { "id": "a4", "field": "salary", "operation": "min", "alias": "minSalary" },
238	            { "id": "a5", "field": "salary", "operation": "max", "alias": "maxSalary" },
239	            { "id": "a6", "field": "name", "operation": "collect", "alias": "names" },
240	            { "id": "a7", "field": "name", "operation": "first", "alias": "firstHire" }
241	          ]
242	        }
243	      }
244	    ]
245	  },
246	  "outputs": {
247	    "output": {
248	      "type": "object",
249	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
250	      "source": "=result.response",
251	      "var": "output"
252	    },
253	    "error": {
254	      "type": "object",

263	**Aggregation operations:**
264

266	| --- | --- | --- |
267	| `count` | Number of items in group | No |
268	| `sum` | Sum of numeric field | Yes |
269	| `average` | Average of numeric field | Yes |
270	| `min` | Minimum value | Yes |
271	| `max` | Maximum value | Yes |

278	## Debug
279	
280	| Error | Cause | Fix |
281	| --- | --- | --- |
282	| Filter passes all items through | Wrong condition name (e.g. `greater` instead of `greater_than`) | Use exact names: `equals`, `not_equals`, `greater_than`, `less_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_equal`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `is_null`, `is_not_null` |
283	| Filter silently returns empty array | Filter `value` holds an unresolved expression (`"$vars.x"`, `"=js:..."`, `"{$vars.x}"`) — Transform compares each item against that string literal | Replace with a literal scalar (`"value": 500`); expressions are not evaluated in filter `value`. If the threshold must be dynamic, do the filter in a Script node |
284	| Collection is null/empty | `collection` was wrapped in `=js:` or set to an inline array literal instead of a plain variable path | Use a path such as `"$vars.loadCatalog.output.catalog"` or `"$vars.catalog"`; keep static arrays in a variable default or upstream node |

1	# HTTP Request Node — Manual Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when there is no IS connector for the target service, the API needs no auth (or auth you pass yourself in headers), or you are prototyping against an arbitrary REST endpoint. For connector-managed auth, use [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) instead.
4	
5	**No connection lookup required.** Manual mode uses `ImplicitConnection` — there are no IS bindings.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–4 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	> **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` to set `parentId`. Without it, the node runs outside the loop context and outputs are null. See [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
17	
18	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Step 2 reuses it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 2 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
19	
20	## Step 2 — Configure the node
21	
22	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …). See [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md).
23	
24	```bash
25	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
26	  --detail '{
27	    "authentication": "manual",
28	    "method": "GET",
29	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
30	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
31	  }' --output json
32	```
33	
34	The CLI:
35	
36	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (manual auth, `ImplicitConnection`, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
37	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither
38	
39	`url` must be a full URL (scheme + host + path). For auth headers you control, pass them under `headers`:
40	
41	```bash
42	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
43	  --detail '{
44	    "authentication": "manual",
45	    "method": "GET",
46	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
47	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
48	  }' --output json
49	```
50	
51	**Dynamic values:** HTTP input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
52	
53	## Step 3 — (Optional) Response branches
54	
55	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 4 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
56	
57	## Step 4 — Wire edges
58	
59	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 3 entry). Wire `default` to the next node. Wire `error` to a handler **only when the requirements say what a failed call should do** — with no `error` edge the call faults the flow, which is the correct default, and setting `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` without the edge swallows the failure into a run that reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
60	
61	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
62	
63	## Debug
64	
65	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For manual mode, watch for `ImplicitConnection` errors — they signal a missing `authentication: "manual"` flag or a non-URL `url` value.

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |
